skill.name: dev-servers
skill.description: Start the backend (FastAPI/uvicorn) and frontend (Vite) development servers. Use when user mentions "start dev", "run servers", "launch app", "start the app", or needs to run the application locally.
skill.summary: Start FastAPI and Vite development servers for local application work.
skill.author: AppleLamps

security_audit.summary: The skill is a local development helper that uses Bash to install dependencies and start FastAPI and Vite servers. Several Markdown backtick and localhost URL detections are false positives, but package installation, project script execution, and .env checks are real operational risks. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Package installation commands can execute dependency or lifecycle scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and show the exact working directory and command before running pip install or npm install.

remediation.issue: Development server commands execute project code and open local ports.
remediation.suggestion: Bind services to localhost, check port conflicts first, and warn users before running project scripts.

remediation.issue: The .env check references OPENAI_API_KEY and may touch a sensitive file.
remediation.suggestion: Check only for file existence and variable presence without printing, copying, or logging secret values.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 11 uses Markdown backticks around the backend/venv/ path. It describes a directory existence check and does not instruct shell execution.
Line 12 uses Markdown backticks around the frontend/node_modules/ path. It is a dependency directory check, not a Ruby or shell backtick execution pattern.
Line 15 instructs Bash to run pip install from the backend directory. Installing project dependencies can execute setup code or install untrusted packages.
Line 16 instructs Bash to run npm install in the frontend directory. npm install can run package lifecycle scripts from project dependencies.
Line 19 instructs Bash to run uvicorn and execute backend application code. This is legitimate for the skill but still starts a local service from project code.
Line 20 instructs Bash to run the frontend dev script. This executes package.json scripts and starts a local service from the project.
Line 22 uses Markdown backticks around .env and OPENAI_API_KEY. It does not contain a shell command or command substitution.
The URL on line 19 is http://localhost:8000 for a local backend dev server. It does not indicate external network communication or data exfiltration.
The URL on line 20 is http://localhost:5173 for a local Vite dev server. It is loopback-only context, not an external endpoint.
Line 22 asks the agent to verify that backend/.env contains OPENAI_API_KEY. This touches secret-bearing configuration, although the skill does not request disclosure.
Line 30 is a protective guardrail that says not to expose or log OPENAI_API_KEY. It does not instruct the agent to read, print, or transmit the secret.
Line 22 requires checking backend/.env for a key name, which involves a sensitive environment file. The risk is credential exposure if the check is implemented by printing file contents.

content.value_statement: Local full-stack projects often need backend and frontend servers started in the right order. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through dependency checks, setup, and local server launch steps.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether backend/venv/ exists before backend setup.
Checks whether frontend/node_modules/ exists before frontend setup.
Guides backend dependency installation with pip when dependencies are missing.
Guides frontend dependency installation with npm when dependencies are missing.
Starts a FastAPI backend with uvicorn on localhost port 8000.
Starts a Vite frontend server on localhost port 5173.
limitations: Assumes the project uses backend and frontend directories.
Assumes the backend entry point is main:app.
Does not create an OPENAI_API_KEY or manage account credentials.
Uses fixed default ports unless the user changes the commands.

best_practices: Confirm before installing dependencies or running project scripts.
Check local ports before starting servers.
Verify secret presence without printing secret values.
anti_patterns: Do not print backend/.env contents to confirm configuration.
Do not run npm install or pip install without user approval.
Do not assume ports 8000 and 5173 are free.

faq.question: What applications does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports projects with a FastAPI backend and a Vite frontend using the expected directory layout.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to confirm with the user before installing missing dependencies.

faq.question: Does it expose my OPENAI_API_KEY?
faq.answer: No. The skill says never to expose or log the key, but secret checks should avoid printing file contents.

faq.question: Which ports does it use?
faq.answer: The backend uses localhost port 8000, and the frontend uses localhost port 5173 by default.

faq.question: Can it fix port conflicts?
faq.answer: It can warn when the default ports are in use, but changing ports may require project-specific commands.

faq.question: Can it run production servers?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for local development servers, not production deployment.
